fields.description:
## The defect

`REBAR_MCP_READONLY=` (set to the EMPTY STRING) silently overrides an explicit
`[mcp] readonly = true` in `rebar.toml` and brings the MCP server up with its full write surface.
No error, no warning. Every OTHER malformed value is loud.

## Reproduced by me, independently, against current `origin/main`

With a `rebar.toml` containing `[mcp]\nreadonly = true`:

```
REBAR_MCP_READONLY unset      -> mcp_readonly() = True    (file honoured)
REBAR_MCP_READONLY=''         -> mcp_readonly() = False   <-- file DEFEATED, silently
REBAR_MCP_READONLY='  '       -> mcp_readonly() = False
REBAR_MCP_READONLY='garbage'  -> ConfigError: cannot resolve the MCP read-only gate ... (loud)
REBAR_MCP_READONLY='false'    -> mcp_readonly() = False   (correct, explicit)
```

## Mechanism, verified in source

- `src/rebar/_config_coercion.py` — `_FALSE = {"false", "0", "no", "off", ""}`. The empty string is
  an accepted spelling of False.
- `src/rebar/_config_sources.py:398` — the env override gates on key PRESENCE (`if name in
  os.environ`), not on the value being non-empty. So `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=` enters the layer stack
  as `""`, and env outranks the file.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:158` — `if ctx.readonly():` returns early and registers NO write tools.
  So the gate genuinely controls the write surface; this is not a cosmetic flag.

This directly defeats the stated contract of `config.mcp_readonly()`, which documents itself as
fail-loud per operator ruling `39f8-ae7c`: *"a fault must error, never silently resolve to a
default, even a safe one"*. The empty string is the one input that resolves silently — and it
resolves in the UNSAFE direction.

## The asymmetry is what makes it a trap

Both gates coerce `""` to `False`. But `False` means opposite things:

```
config: [mcp] readonly = true, allow_llm = true
REBAR_MCP_READONLY=''   -> readonly=False  allow_llm=True    <-- protection OFF
REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=''  -> readonly=True   allow_llm=False   <-- capability OFF (safe)
```

So the identical operator mistake is harmless on one gate and disables a security control on the
other. Anyone reasoning "an empty env var is the same as unset" is right for `allow_llm` and wrong
for `readonly`.

## EXPOSURE: latent, NOT live — stated plainly because it changes the priority

I checked the deployment before filing. **`REBAR_MCP_READONLY` is not set at all in
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`**, and the only two places that set it —
`.github/workflows/jira-dc-richtext-probe.yml:105` and `jira-dc-capability-map.yml:109` — pass a
literal `"1"`. There is no `${VAR}` indirection on it anywhere in `infra/` or `.github/`.

So no live instance exists today. The reported trigger (`REBAR_MCP_READONLY=${MCP_RO}` in a
compose/systemd/k8s env block with `MCP_RO` unset) is a plausible FUTURE shape, not the current
one. This is a latent footgun in a security control, filed at p2 on that basis rather than p1.

## Compounding (verify before relying on it — I did not reproduce this half)

The sweep also reported `_config_sources.py` testing `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS == "error"` only,
so `strict`/`fail`/`1`/`true`/`yes` would all silently degrade to WARN — meaning an operator's
attempt to make unknown keys loud is itself ineffective, and a typo'd `mcp.read_only` would be
dropped with a log line while the server comes up writable. I have NOT verified that half; treat
it as an unproven lead and confirm it before designing around it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `REBAR_MCP_READONLY=` (empty) does NOT silently disable the read-only gate. Whether it
      raises, or is treated as unset, is a design decision — make it deliberately and record the
      reasoning; do not just add `""` to `_TRUE`.
- [x] Whatever is chosen applies to the SECURITY-DIRECTION gates as a class, not just this one
      key. Enumerate every boolean config gate whose `False` means "protection off" and state each
      one's disposition — fixing only `readonly` leaves the next one to be found the same way.
- [x] `allow_llm` and other capability gates keep their current safe behaviour on `""`. A fix that
      makes an empty string raise everywhere may be right, but confirm it does not break the
      deliberate "unset means denied" posture those gates rely on.
- [x] A regression test drives the real resolver (not a stub) with `""`, `"  "`, unset, and a
      malformed value against a file that sets the opposite, and pins each outcome. Seed the
      defect by reverting the fix and confirm the test goes RED — an assertion that passes both
      before and after would be this ticket's own bug class.
- [x] The empty-string coercion is examined once across ALL config keys, and any other key where
      `""` resolves in an unsafe direction is listed with its disposition.
